speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help identify the cause, please describe your symptoms: do you feel like you or your surroundings are spinning, does it happen when you change position, and how long do the episodes last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the positional nature of your vertigo, have you noticed any new hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness in the affected ear during these episodes? REQUEST TEST: Audiometry.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any visual disturbances such as double vision, drooping eyelids, or difficulty speaking, and have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your limbs? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain (Posterior Fossa); REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: No evidence of central lesions or infarcts that would suggest central causes of vertigo.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms this is not a central issue like a stroke; since your vertigo is position-dependent and your brain imaging is normal, I suspect Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Have you noticed any nausea or vomiting during these episodes, and do you have a history of head trauma or ear infections? REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike Manoeuvre: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), likely affecting the posterior semicircular canal on the right side.
